cues.en: It's a privilege to be engaged in a conversation with my colleague Elizabeth Spelke. We go back a long way. We've been colleagues both at MIT, where I helped attract her, and at Harvard, where she helped attract me. Like most people in my field, I have enormous admiration for Liz's brilliant contributions to our understanding of the origins of cognition.
cues.zh: 能与我的同事伊丽莎白·斯佩尔克（Elizabeth Spelke）展开对话，我深感荣幸。我们交情匪浅。我们在麻省理工学院共事过，当时是我把她挖过去的；后来在哈佛大学，她又把我吸引了过去。和我们领域的多数人一样，我对莉兹在认知起源理解上的卓越贡献怀有无比的敬意。

cues.en: But we do find ourselves with somewhat different perspectives on a recent issue. And for those of you who just arrived from Mars, there's been a certain amount of discussion here at Harvard on a particular datum. And that is the underrepresentation of women among tenure-track faculty in elite universities in physical science, math, and engineering. And here are some recent figures.
cues.zh: 但对于最近的一个议题，我们确实发现彼此的观点略有不同。对于那些刚从火星来到这里的人来说，最近哈佛大学围绕某个具体数据展开了不少讨论。这就是：在顶尖大学的物理科学、数学和工程学领域中，终身轨道教职员工中女性的比例偏低。以下是一些最近的数据。

cues.en: As with many issues in psychology, there are three broad classes of explanations. One can imagine an extreme nature position that males but not females have the talents and temperaments necessary for science. Needless to say, only a madman could believe that and there aren't any proponents of that position. There's an extreme nurture position that males and females are biologically indistinguishable and all the relevant sex differences are products of socialization and bias.
cues.zh: 正如心理学中的许多问题一样，大致有三类解释。我们可以设想一种极端的先天论立场，即只有男性而非女性才具备从事科学研究的天赋和气质。不用说，只有疯子才会相信这一点，而且也没有人支持这种立场。还有一种极端的后天论立场，即男性和女性在生物学上没有区别，所有相关的性别差异都是社会化和偏见产物。

cues.en: And then there's an intermediate position that the difference is explainable by some combination of biological differences in average temperaments and talents interacting with socialization and bias. Well, Liz has embraced the extreme nurture position, ironically enough, because standardly, in cognitive science, she and I are always put in the same camp as the innateists when it comes to explaining the mind. But Liz has said that there is not a shred of evidence for the biological factor,
cues.zh: 接着还有一种折中立场，即这种差异可以通过平均气质和天赋的生物学差异与社会化及偏见相互作用的某种组合来解释。然而，莉兹却接受了极端的后天论立场，这具有相当的讽刺意味，因为在认知科学中，通常在解释心灵时，她和我总是被归入先天论的同一个阵营。但莉兹曾表示，没有一丝证据表明存在生物学因素，

cues.en: that the case against there being a male advantage is so overwhelming that it is hard to see how one can make a case for it on the other side and that this is as conclusive as any finding that I know of in science. Well, we certainly aren't facing the stereotypical gender difference in confidence here. I'm a controversial guy. I've taken a lot of controversial positions over the years and as a member of Homo Sapiens, I think I'm right on all of them.
cues.zh: 认为反对男性优势的论据是如此压倒性，以至于很难看出另一方如何能为之辩护，并称这与我所知道的科学发现一样具有决定性。好吧，我们在这里肯定没有遇到那种刻板的自信心性别差异。我是一个颇具争议的人。这些年来我持过许多充满争议的立场，而且作为智人的一员，我认为自己在所有这些立场上都是对的。

cues.en: But on the other hand, I don't think that in any of them, I would say that there's not a shred of evidence for the other side that even if I think the evidence favors one side, I would not say that the other side can't even make a case even if I think that their case is not as good as the opposite. And as conclusive as any finding in science, I mean, this is social science. This would imply that the
cues.zh: 但另一方面，我不认为在其中任何一个观点上，我会说另一方完全没有任何证据——即使我认为证据倾向于某一方，我也不会说另一方连一点道理都讲不通，哪怕我认为他们的论点不如对立面那么好。而且，要达到科学中任何发现那样确凿的程度，我的意思是，这是社会科学。这就意味着，

cues.en: extreme nurture position is more convincing than say the evidence that the Sun is at the center of the solar system or the laws of thermodynamics, theory of evolution, plate tectonics, and so on. I think these are rather extreme statements. Especially in light of the fact that there is an enormous amount of work summarized in these and many other literature reviews that in fact come to a very different conclusion. And I'll cite
cues.zh: 极端后天决定论比诸如太阳位于太阳系中心、热力学定律、进化论、板块构造论等证据更具说服力。我认为这些都是相当极端的说法。特别是考虑到有大量的工作被总结在这些以及许多其他的文献综述中，事实上它们得出了非常不同的结论。我将引用

cues.en: from one of them, a book called Sex Differences and Cognitive Abilities by Diane Halpern, a respected psychologist, recently elected president of the APA, and someone with no theoretical axe to grind certainly does not subscribe to any particular theory, and has been a critic, for example, of evolutionary psychology. And here's what she wrote in the preface to her book. At the time I started writing this book, it seemed clear to me that any between sex differences and thinking abilities were due to socialization practices, artifacts,
cues.zh: 其中一篇文献，一本名为《性别的差异与认知能力》（Sex Differences and Cognitive Abilities）的书，作者是 Diane Halpern，一位受人尊敬的心理学家、最近当选的 APA 主席，她没有需要维护的理论私心，当然也不盲从任何特定理论，并且一直是例如进化科学的批评者。以下是她在书的前言中写的内容：在我开始写这本书的时候，我很清楚地认为，思维能力上的任何性别差异都是由社会化实践、研究人为因素、

cues.en: and mistakes in the research. After reviewing a pile of journal articles that stood several feet high and numerous books and book chapters that dwarfed the stack of journal articles, I changed my mind. The literature on sex differences and cognitive abilities is filled with inconsistent findings, contradictory theories, and emotional claims that are unsupported by the research. Yet despite all the noise in the data, clear and consistent messages could be heard. There are real and in some cases sizable sex differences with respect to some cognitive abilities.
cues.zh: 以及研究中的错误造成的。在审阅了高达几英尺的期刊论文堆，以及让期刊论文相形见绌的无数书籍和章节之后，我改变了主意。关于性别差异与认知能力的文献充斥着不一致的发现、矛盾的理论以及不获研究支持的情感化主张。然而，尽管数据中存在诸多杂音，清晰且一致的信息依然能够被听见。在某些认知能力方面，确实存在真实的、在某些情况下甚至相当显著的性别差异。

cues.en: Socialization practices are undoubtedly important, but there is also good evidence that biological sex differences play a role in establishing and maintaining cognitive sex differences, a conclusion I wasn't prepared to make when I began reviewing the relevant literature. This captures my assessment perfectly. Now, again, for the benefit of the Martians in this room, this isn't just any old issue in empirical psychology, and there are some
cues.zh: 社交化实践无疑很重要，但也有充分的证据表明，在形成和维持认知上的两性差异方面，生物学上的性别差异也发挥了作用——当我开始查阅相关文献时，我还没准备好得出这个结论。这句话完美概括了我的评估。现在，再次说明，为了照顾在座各位“火星人”（对情况不了解的人），这可不是实证心理学中什么无关紧要的陈旧问题，而且其中还带有某些

cues.en: political colourings to it, and so I want to begin with just a confession of my own politics. That is, I am a feminist. I believe that women have been oppressed and discriminated against and harassed for thousands of years. I believe that the
cues.zh: 政治色彩，所以我想先坦白一下我自己的政治立场。也就是说，我是一个女权主义者。我相信女性在数千年来一直受到压迫、歧视和骚扰。我坚信

cues.en: Two waves of the feminist movement in the 20th century are among the proudest achievements in our species. I'm happy to have lived through one of them, and including the effort to increase representation of women in the sciences. But in order to endorse this claim, I think it's crucial to distinguish between the moral proposition
cues.zh: 20世纪的两次女权主义浪潮是我们物种最值得骄傲的成就之一。我很庆幸自己经历其中一次，包括为提高女性在科学领域的代表性所做出的努力。但为了支持这一主张，我认为至关重要的是要区分以下两点：其一是道德命题，即

cues.en: that people should not be discriminated against on account of their sex, which I take to be the core of feminism, and the empirical claim that males and females are biologically indistinguishable. These are not the same thing. Indeed, distinguishing them I think is essential to protecting the core of feminism.
cues.zh: 不应因性别而对人们进行歧视，我认为这是女权主义的核心；其二是实证主张，即男性和女性在生物学上是没有区别的。这两者不是一回事。事实上，我认为区分它们对于捍卫女权主义的核心至关重要。

cues.en: Since anyone who takes an honest interest in science has to be prepared for the facts to come out either way, it's essential that we don't hold the ideals of feminism hostage to the latest findings that come out of the lab or field, which would only result in, if they came out one way, saying that I guess sex discrimination wasn't so bad after all, or else in furiously spin doctoring the scientific results to preserve the political principle.
cues.zh: 既然任何真诚关心科学的人都必须准备好接受事实朝任一方向发展，我们就绝不能让女权主义的理想受制于实验室或实地研究的最新发现，否则只会导致这样的结果：如果发现偏向一方，就说“我猜性别歧视也没那么糟”，或者为了维护政治原则而拼命对科学结果进行spin doctoring。

cues.en: The truth cannot be sexist, and whatever the facts turn out to be, I don't think they compromise the core of feminism. Well, why study sex differences? Believe me, being the Bobby Riggs of cognitive science is not my idea of a good time. And why study them? It's not the focus of my own research, but on the other hand, as a curious person, the difference between the sexes is part of the human condition.
cues.zh: 真相不可能带有性别歧视，无论事实如何，我都不认为它们会损害女权主义的核心。那么，为什么要研究性别差异呢？相信我，成为认知科学界的Bobby Riggs可不是我心目中的好时光。为什么要研究它们？这不是我自己研究的焦点，但另一方面，作为一个好奇的人，性别之间的差异是人类境况的一部分。

cues.en: We all have a mother and a father. Most of us are attracted to members of the opposite sex and the rest of us notice the difference from those who do. And we can't help but notice the sex of our children, friends and colleagues in every walk of life. Also, the topic of sex difference is a great scientific interest. It's a fundamental problem in biology because sex goes back probably a billion years of sex differences.
cues.zh: 我们每个人都有母亲和父亲。我们大多数人都被异性成员吸引，其余的人则注意到与那些被吸引的人的不同。我们不禁注意到自己的孩子、朋友和各行各业同事的性别。此外，性别差异这个话题具有重大的科学意义。这是生物学中的一个基本问题，因为性别差异可能可以追溯到十亿年前。

cues.en: There's an interesting theory, which I won't have time to get into, that predicts that there should be an overall and equal investment of organisms in males and females. Neither sex is predicted to be superior or inferior. But also an elegant theory, Bob Triver's theory of differential minimum parental investment, that makes some highly specific predictions about when you should expect differences. Also, it's of practical importance.
cues.zh: 有一个有趣的理论，我没时间深入探讨，它预测生物体对雄性和雌性的总体投资应该相等。没有哪个性别被预测为优越或低劣。但还有一个优雅的理论，Bob Triver的差异最低亲代投资理论，它对何时应该预期差异做出了高度具体的预测。此外，它还具有实际重要性。

cues.en: I think there are aspects of the world that we want to change but if we want to change the world we must first understand it and that includes understanding the sources of sex differences. So let me get back to the datum to be explained. In many ways this is a very exotic phenomenon. It involves biologically unprepared talents and temperaments. Evolution certainly did not shape any part of the mind in order to be a professor of mechanical engineering at MIT for example.
cues.zh: 我认为世界有些方面是我们想改变的，但要想改变世界，必须先理解它，这包括理解性别差异的来源。那么让我回到那个待解释的数据点。这个现象在很多方面都非常奇特。它涉及生物学上未经准备的天赋和性情。比如，进化肯定没有为了让人成为MIT机械工程教授而塑造大脑的任何部分。

cues.en: And so the datum has nothing to do with basic cognitive processes or those that we use in our everyday lives, in school or even in most college courses where indeed there are few sex differences. So this datum is not about that kind of performance. We're also talking about extremes of achievement. Most women are not qualified to be math professors at Harvard because most men aren't qualified to be math professors at Harvard.
cues.zh: 所以这个数据点与基本认知过程无关，也与我们在日常生活中、学校里甚至大多数大学课程中使用的能力无关——在这些领域，性别差异其实很小。所以这个数据点不是关于那类表现的。我们谈的是成就的极端情况。大多数女性没有资格成为哈佛的数学教授，因为大多数男性也没有资格。

cues.en: We are talking about extremes in the population. We're talking about a subset of fields that it is not the case that women are underrepresented to that extent in all academic fields and certainly not in all prestigious professions. And also we're talking about a statistical effect. This is such a crucial point that I want to discuss it in some detail. Women are nowhere near absent even from the fields in which they are underrepresented.
cues.zh: 我们谈的是人群中的极端情况。我们谈的是某些领域的子集——并非所有学术领域都存在那种程度的女性代表性不足，当然也并非所有有声望的职业都如此。而且我们谈的是一个统计效应。这一点非常关键，我想稍作详细讨论。即便在女性代表性不足的领域，女性也远未缺席。

cues.en: And the explanations for differences must be statistical as well. And here is just a touchstone for this entire discussion. These are two Gaussian or normal distributions, bell curves, where this is anything that you want to measure. The x-axis, the y-axis is the proportion of people at that ability. This is what it typically...
cues.zh: 而且对差异的解释也必须是统计学上的。这里只是整场讨论的一个试金石。这是两个高斯或正态分布，也就是钟形曲线，这里的横轴可以是你想测量的任何东西，纵轴则是具备该能力的人口比例。这通常就是……

cues.en: looks like when you compare the sexes on any measure in which they differ. Mainly, if we, for this example, if we say that this is the male curve and this is the female curve, the means may be different, but at any particular level of the variable, there are always representatives of both genders. So, right away, a number of
cues.zh: 当你比较两性在任何有差异的指标上的表现时，呈现出的样子。主要是，如果我们以这个为例，假设这是男性曲线，这是女性曲线，均值可能不同，但在该变量的任何特定水平上，总是同时存在着两个性别的代表。所以，立刻就会发现，过去几个月里发生的一些事情中的许多

cues.en: statements that have been made in the events of the last couple of months are simply red herrings that should not have been made by people who understand this, such as the accusation that, for example, President Summers implied that 50% of the brightest minds in America do not have the right aptitude for science, that women just can't cut it, and so on. These are statistically illiterate and have nothing to do with what we're actually discussing.
cues.zh: 言论纯粹是烟雾弹，懂行的人根本不该说出这种话，比如有人指控萨默斯校长暗示全美最聪明的头脑中有 50% 没有从事科学的正确资质，女性就是不行，诸如此类。这些都是统计学上的文盲言论，跟我们实际讨论的内容毫无关系。

cues.en: Now, an important corollary of two overlapping normal distributions, one of them is that the normal distribution falls off according to the negative exponential of the square of the difference from the mean. And that means that even with small differences in the means of two distributions, the more extreme the score, the greater the disparity in the numbers. That is, the ratios get more extreme as you go farther out along the tail. If we hold the magnifying glass up to the
cues.zh: 现在，两个重叠的正态分布有一个重要的推论，那就是正态分布的衰减速度遵循与均值差平方的负指数成正比的规律。这意味着，即使两个分布的均值只有微小差异，分数越极端，数量上的差距就会越大。也就是说，当你沿着尾部向外延伸时，比例会变得更加极端。如果我们把放大镜对准

cues.en: tails of the distribution, even though they overlap over the bulk of the curve, when you get out to the extremes, the difference between the two curves gets larger and larger. Which means, to give you an example, we know that the distribution of height between men and women overlap. It's not the case that all men are taller than all women. And at 5'10", there are 30 men for every woman, whereas at 6', there are 2,000 men for every woman.
cues.zh: 分布的尾部，尽管它们在曲线的主体部分重叠，但当你走到极端区域时，两条曲线之间的差距就会越来越大。这意味着，举个例子，我们知道男女的身高分布是重叠的。并非所有男性都比所有女性高。在 5尺10寸 的身高下，每位女性对应 30 名男性；而在 6尺 的身高下，每位女性则对应 2000 名男性。

cues.en: Now the sex differences in cognition tend not to be anything like that but that's just to reinforce the statistical point. Another important corollary is the tail ratios are affected by differences in variance and biologists since Darwin have noted that for many traits and many species males are the more variable gender. So even in cases where the mean for say women and the mean for men is the same the fact that there are more
cues.zh: 现在认知中的性别差异往往并非如此，但这只是为了强调统计学上的观点。另一个重要的推论是，尾部比例会受到方差差异的影响，而达尔文以来的生物学家已经注意到，对于许多特征和许多物种来说，男性是变异更大的性别。因此，即使在例如女性平均值和男性平均值相同的情况下，由于更多

cues.en: men dispersed at the extremes means that at the tails the proportion of men would be higher at one tail and higher at the other as it sometimes summarized that more prodigies, more idiots. So let me begin with the first point in connecting the political issue to the scientific issue and that is that as economists who study
cues.zh: 的男性分散在极端值，这意味着在两端尾部，一端男性的比例会更高，另一端男性比例也会更高，正如有时总结的那样：天才更多，笨蛋也更多。因此，让我从第一点开始，将政治问题与科学问题联系起来，那就是正如研究歧视模式的经济学家长期以来一直争论的那样，往往徒劳无功，差异与歧视之间存在着至关重要的概念差异。

cues.en: patterns of discrimination have long argued, often to no avail, there's a crucial conceptual difference between a difference and discrimination. That a departure from a 50-50 ratio in any profession does not by itself imply discrimination unless the interests and aptitudes are statistically equated. And let me just illustrate that with an example, and I'll use myself. I am in a field that is, in fact,
cues.zh: 任何行业中偏离 50 对 50 的比例本身并不意味着存在歧视，除非在统计上平衡了兴趣和资质。让我用一个例子来阐述这一点，我会拿我自己举例。我所处的领域实际上是

cues.en: dominated by women. 75% of the main professional association in the study of child language is female as are majority of the keynote speakers at our main conference. I'm here to tell you that it's not because I was discriminated against. I decided to study language development as opposed to say mechanical engineering for many reasons.
cues.zh: 由女性主导的。儿童语言研究主要专业协会中 75% 的成员是女性，我们主要会议的主旨发言人多数也是女性。我在这里告诉大家，这并不是因为我受到了歧视。我决定研究语言发展而不是机械工程，是有很多原因的。

cues.en: don't think that designing a better automobile transmission would turn me on as much as figuring out how kids acquire language. And I don't think I'd be as good at it as I am at studying child language. Now, all we need to do in order to explain differences without presumably getting anyone upset about possible sexist interpretation is to ask whether whatever traits that I have
cues.zh: 别以为设计更好的汽车变速箱会像搞懂孩子如何习得语言那样让我兴奋。我也不认为我在这件事上会比研究儿童语言更擅长。现在，要解释差异而又不至于让任何人因可能的性别歧视解读而不快，我们只需问：我身上那些让我有这种倾向的特质

cues.en: that give me that predisposition are exactly equally distributed statistically among men and among women. For all those of you out there who also are not mechanical engineers, then you should understand what I'm talking about, are both genders. Okay, there are many similarities between the sexes. There are no differences in general intelligence or, gee, they are exactly the same on the money.
cues.zh: 是否在男女之间统计上完全均等分布。在场那些也不是机械工程师的人，应该能明白我在说什么——两种性别都是。好，两性之间有很多相似之处。一般智力上没有差异，天哪，在钱上完全一样。

cues.en: Basic categories of cognition, how we negotiate our world and live our everyday life, our concept of objects, number of people, living things and so on, show no differences. And indeed, in cases where there are differences, there's pretty much as many instances in which men do slightly better than women as in which women do slightly better than men. Just to give you a few examples, men are better at throwing, women are more dexterous.
cues.zh: 认知的基本分类、我们如何应对世界和过日常生活、我们对物体、人数、生物等的概念，都没有差异。而且确实，在有差异的情况下，男性略优于女性的例子和女性略优于男性的例子差不多一样多。举几个例子：男性更擅长投掷，女性更灵巧。

cues.en: men are better at mentally rotating shapes, women are better at visual memory, men are better at problem solving, women are better at mathematical calculation, and on and on and on. But there are six differences that are relevant to this data. And the literature on this is so enormous that I can only touch a fraction of it. And I'll restrict myself to a few cases where there are enormous data sets or meta-analyses that
cues.zh: 男性更擅长心理旋转形状，女性更擅长视觉记忆，男性更擅长解决问题，女性更擅长数学计算，等等等等。但有六个差异与这些数据相关。相关文献浩如烟海，我只能触及一小部分。我会局限于少数几个有大量数据集或元分析、

cues.en: try to boil down the literature. The first difference, long noted by economists studying employment patterns, is that many women differ in what they state are their own priorities in life. That, to sum it up, men on average are more likely to chase status at the expense of family. Women give a different weighting. Now, again, think statistics. It doesn't mean that women
cues.zh: 试图浓缩文献的案例。第一个差异，研究就业模式的经济学家早已注意到，是许多女性在她们自述的人生优先事项上有所不同。概括来说，男性平均更可能以家庭为代价追逐地位。女性的权重不同。再说一遍，想想统计学。这并不意味着女性

cues.en: value family and not status. It doesn't mean that men value status and not family, nor does it mean that every last woman or every last man has this asymmetry. But in large data sets, on average, that's what you find. And just one example of this is in the study of mathematically precocious youth. In this case, 1,729 people who were selected in seventh grade for being in the top 1% of ability in mathematics
cues.zh: 重视家庭而不重视地位。也不意味着男性重视地位而不重视家庭，也不意味着每一个女性或每一个男性都有这种不对称。但在大数据集中，平均而言，你会发现就是这样。一个例子是数学早慧青少年的研究。该研究中，1729人在七年级时因数学能力位居前1%而被选中

cues.en: These are men and women who are then followed up decades later. They are certainly equally talented. If anyone has ever been encouraged at math and science, these kids were both genders. They are equal in terms of their levels of achievement and they report being equally satisfied with the course of their lives. Nonetheless, there are a number of statistical differences in what they say is important to them.
cues.zh: 这些人是男是女，在几十年后会受到持续跟踪调查。他们的天赋绝对不相上下。如果说有人曾在数学和科学方面受到过鼓励，这些孩子不论男女都是如此。他们在成就水平上不相上下，并且都表示对自己的生活历程感到同样满意。尽管如此，在他们认为重要的事情上，还是存在一些统计学上的差异。

cues.en: There are a number of cases in which females rate things higher than males, such as the ability to have a part-time career for a limited time in one's life, living close to parents and relatives, having a meaningful spiritual life, having strong friendships. For the traits that men rate as higher than women on average, they include having lots of money, inventing or creating something, having a full-time career, being successful in my line of work.
cues.zh: 在许多情况下，女性的评分高于男性，例如在人生的某个有限阶段拥有兼职职业的能力、与父母和亲戚住得近、拥有有意义的精神生活、拥有深厚的友谊。至于男性平均评分高于女性的特质，则包括拥有很多钱、发明或创造某样东西、拥有全职职业、在我的专业领域取得成功。

cues.en: And it's worth noting that studies of highly successful people note that single-mindedness and competitiveness is a recurring trait in geniuses of both sexes. And here's just one other figure from this data set. As you might expect, this sample has a lot of people who like to work herculean hours, a lot of people who like to work 50, 60, even 70 hours a week.
cues.zh: 值得一提的是，对极具成功的人士的研究表明，专一和好胜心是男女两性天才身上共同的经常性特征。这里还有来自该数据集的另一个数字。正如你所料，这个样本中有很多人喜欢付出超常的工作时间，有很多人喜欢每周工作 50、60 甚至 70 个小时。

cues.en: But there are slight differences at each one of these ranges. There are slightly more men than women who want to don't care whether or not they have a life. Second, people versus things and abstract rule systems. There is a staggering amount of data on this because there's a whole field of psychology and economics that studies people's vocational interests. I bet most people in this room have taken one of those tests at some point in their lives. And there are...
cues.zh: 但在每一个这样的区间，都存在细微的差异。想要或者不在乎自己有没有个人生活的男性，比女性略多一些。第二，人与物以及抽象规则系统。关于这一点有海量的数据，因为有一个完整的心理学和经济学领域专门研究人们的职业兴趣。我敢说在座的大多数人在人生的某个阶段都做过其中某种测试。还有……

cues.en: consistent differences in the kinds of things that appeal to men and women in their ideal job. I'll just discuss one of them, which is a desire to work with people versus things where there is an enormous, that is a one standard deviation in terms of men over women. And indeed this will tend to cause people to gravitate in slightly different directions.
cues.zh: 在理想职业中，吸引男性和女性的东西存在一致性差异。我只谈其中一点，即与人打交道还是与事物打交道的意愿，这里存在巨大的差异，即男性比女性高出一个标准差。这确实会倾向于促使人们向略微不同的方向靠拢。

cues.en: For the occupation that's strongest at the people end of this continuum is a director of a community services organization. The occupations that are strongest at the things end are physicist, chemist, mathematician, computer programmer, and biologist. And you see this not only in choice of whether to go into science,
cues.zh: 在这个连续体上最偏向“与人打交道”一端的职业是社区服务组织的主任。最偏向“与事物打交道”一端的职业是物理学家、化学家、数学家、计算机程序员和生物学家。你不仅能在是否进入科学领域的选择上看到这一点，

cues.en: but also in which branch of science the sexes go into. Needless to say, from 1970 to 2002 there's been a huge increase in the percentage of degrees awarded to women.
cues.zh: 还能在兩性进入科学哪个分支上看到。不用说，从1970年到2002年，授予女性的学位比例大幅增加。

cues.en: But among the PhDs, for example, you find a difference. We'll take the year 2001 that in education, 65% of the doctorates go to women, 54% of social science degrees, 47% of life science, 26% of physical science, 17% of engineering, which is perfectly predictable by the continuum between people and living things and inanimate objects. And this is pretty much the same in 1980 and 2001, despite changes in absolute numbers.
cues.zh: 但例如在博士中，你会发现差异。以2001年为例，教育领域65%的博士授予女性，社会科学学位占54%，生命科学占47%，物理科学占26%，工程学占17%，这完全可以通过人与生物和无生命物体之间的连续体来预测。尽管绝对数量有变化，1980年和2001年的情况大体相同。

cues.en: Third, risk. Men are by far the more reckless sex. In a large meta-analysis involving 150 studies and 100,000 participants, in 14 out of 16 categories of risk-taking, men were over-represented. The two sexes were equal and the other two, one of which was smoking for obvious reasons. And two of the largest sex differences were in intellectual risk-taking and participation in a risky experiment.
cues.zh: 第三，风险。男性是远为更鲁莽的性别。在一项涉及150项研究和10万名参与者的大型元分析中，在16个风险承担类别中的14个里，男性占比过高。两个性别相等，另外两个中有一个是吸烟，原因显而易见。而最大的两个性别差异之一在于智力风险承担和参与有风险的实验。

cues.en: And I think it's because of this that we, in everyday life, we do see such a difference. Men are very much overrepresented in the following category, namely the Darwin Awards, commemorating those individuals who ensure the long-term survival of our species by removing themselves from the gene pool in a sublimely idiotic fashion, in which I think virtually all, perhaps all of the winners are men. Fourth, three-dimensional mental transformations, the ability to determine whether
cues.zh: 我想也正是因为这一点，我们在日常生活中才会看到如此明显的差异。男性在以下这个类别中占比极高，也就是达尔文奖，该奖项旨在纪念那些以极其愚蠢的方式把自己从基因库中剔除，从而确保我们物种长期生存的人，我认为几乎所有，也许所有的获奖者都是男性。第四，三维心理转化，即判断……的能力

cues.en: Each of these pairs of objects represents the same three-dimensional shape. Again, I'll appeal to a meta-analysis, 286 data sets, 100,000 subjects, and the authors say we have specified a number of tests that show highly significant sex differences that are stable across age, at least after puberty, and have not decreased in recent years. In this case,
cues.zh: 每一对这样的物体都代表着相同的三维形状。再次引用一项元分析，涵盖286个数据集、10万名受试者，作者表示：我们指定了多项测试，显示出显著的性别差异，这些差异在不同年龄段（至少在青春期之后）保持稳定，并且近年来没有减少。在这种情况下，

cues.en: test, the advantage goes to the men, although as I mentioned, the advantage goes to women in other kinds of spatial ability. But in mental rotation, spatial perception, and spatial visualization, there are sex differences tipping in the male direction. Now, does this have any relevance to scientific achievement? Well, we don't really know for sure, but there's some reason to think that it is, that three-dimensional
cues.zh: 测试中，男性的优势更明显，不过正如我所提到的，女性在其他种类的空间能力上占有优势。但在心理旋转、空间知觉和空间可视化方面，性别差异偏向男性一方。那么，这与科学成就有任何关联吗？嗯，我们并不是十分确定，但有一些理由认为是的，三维

cues.en: spatial visualization is correlated with mathematical problem solving, and it figures prominently in the memoirs and introspections of most creative physicists and chemists, including Faraday, Maxwell, Tesla, Kekele, and Lawrence, all of whom claim to have hit upon their discoveries by
cues.zh: 空间可视化与数学问题解决能力相关，它在大多数富有创造力的物理学家和化学家的回忆录和内省中占有重要地位，包括法拉第、麦克斯韦、特斯拉、凯库勒和劳伦斯，他们都声称自己是通过

cues.en: dynamic visual imagery and only later set them down in equations. A typical quote is as follows, the cyclical entities which seem to serve as elements in my thought are certain signs and more or less clear images which can be voluntarily reproduced and combined. This combinatory place seems to be the essential feature in productive thought before there is any connection with logical construction in words or other kinds of signs. And that is a quote from a fairly well-known scientist.
cues.zh: 动态视觉表象取得发现，只是在后来才将其写成方程式。一个典型的引言是这样的：似乎作为我思维中元素的循环实体，是某些符号以及或多或少清晰的图像，它们可以被自愿地重现和组合。这种组合的过程似乎是生产性思维的基本特征，在此之前，它与用词语或其他符号进行的逻辑构建没有任何联系。这段引言来自一位相当著名的科学家。

cues.en: Mathematical reasoning. Girls and women get better school grades in mathematics and pretty much everything else these days. And women are better at mathematical calculation, but consistently men score at least statistically better on mathematical word problems and on tests of mathematical reasoning.
cues.zh: 数学推理。如今，女孩和妇女在学校的数学成绩以及几乎所有其他学科上都表现得更好。而且女性更擅长数学计算，但在数学应用题和数学推理测试中，男性的得分在统计学上始终至少要高一些。

cues.en: Again, a meta-analysis, 254 datasets, 3 million subjects shows no significant difference in childhood. This is a difference that emerges around puberty, but there are sizable differences in adolescence and adulthood, especially in high-end samples. Here is an example of the SAT mathematical score where there is about a 40-point difference in favor of men that's pretty much consistent from 1972 to 1997.
cues.zh: 同样，一项包含 254 个数据集、300 万名被试的元分析显示，在童年期并没有显著差异。这种差异大约在青春期出现，但在青春期和成年期却存在相当大的差异，特别是在高端样本中。这是一个 SAT 数学成绩的例子，男性的优势大约为 40 分，从 1972 年到 1997 年这一直非常稳定。

cues.en: In the study of mathematically precocious youth in which 7th graders were given the SAT, which of course ordinarily is administered only to college bound kids who are much older, the ratio of those scoring over 700 is 2.8 to 1, male to female.
cues.zh: 在对数学天赋异禀的青少年的研究中，让七年级学生参加 SAT 考试（该考试通常只针对年长得多的、准备上大学的孩子），得分在 700 分以上的男女比例是 2.8 比 1。

cues.en: Admittedly and interestingly, that's down from 25 years ago when it was a 13 to 1 ratio, and perhaps we can discuss some of the reasons. At the 760 cutoff, the ratio nowadays is 7 to 1 male to female. Now, why is there a discrepancy with grades? Do SATs and other tests of mathematical reasoning underpredict grades or do grades overpredict high-end aptitude?
cues.zh: 诚然，也有趣的是，这比 25 年前的 13 比 1 的比例有所下降，也许我们可以讨论一下其中的一些原因。在 760 分的截断分上，如今的男女比例是 7 比 1。那么，为什么成绩会出现不一致呢？是 SAT 和其他数学推理测试低估了成绩，还是成绩高估了高端天赋？

cues.en: At the Radcliffe Forum, Liz was very explicit in which side she takes, saying that the tests are no good, unquote. Well, one question is, why does every major graduate program, including MIT and Harvard, the very departments where Liz and I selected our graduate students by looking at GRE scores, still use them if they are so useless? And I think the reason is that compared to school grades in which you are often, which often are affected by homework, by
cues.zh: 在拉德克利夫论坛上，Liz 明确表态支持哪一方，原话是“这些测试毫无用处”。那么，这里有个问题：既然这些测试这么没用，为什么包括麻省理工和哈佛在内的各大顶尖研究生院——也就是 Liz和我当年通过查看 GRE 成绩来选拔研究生的那些系——现在依然在使用它们？我觉得原因在于，学校成绩往往会受到家庭作业的影响，受到

cues.en: solving the kind of problems that have already been presented in lecture and textbooks, the aptitude tests are designed to test the application of mathematical knowledge to unfamiliar problems, which is of course the way that math is used in actually doing math and science. And in fact, I think contrary to popular opinion of Liz and many intellectuals, the tests are very good. There is an enormous amount of data on the predictive power of SAT tests.
cues.zh: 那些在课堂和教科书上已经讲过的问题的干扰；相比之下，能力倾向测试旨在测试如何将数学知识应用于陌生的问题，而这正是数学在实际数学研究和科学工作中的应用方式。事实上，我认为与 Liz 以及许多知识分子的流行看法相反，这些测试非常出色。关于 SAT 测试预测能力的数据极其庞大。

cues.en: Among people in science careers, they overwhelmingly score in the 90th percentile in the SAT or GRAE math, and they predict earnings, occupational choice, doctoral degrees, the prestige of one's degree, the probability of having a tenure-track position, and number of patents. Moreover, this predictive power is the same for men and women.
cues.zh: 在从事科学职业的人群中，他们的 SAT 或 GRE 数学成绩绝大多数都在第 90 百分位以上，而且这些成绩能预测收入、职业选择、博士学位、学位声誉、获得终身教轨教职的概率以及专利数量。此外，这种预测能力在男性和女性身上是一样的。

cues.en: As for why there is that under prediction, slight under prediction, one tenth of a standard deviation in undergraduate grades, the College Board did do a study on that, and they were able to explain it by a combination of the choice of major, which differs among sexes, and the greater conscientiousness of women solving that mystery. Finally, there's variability. Here it's crucial to, because estimates of variance
cues.zh: 至于为什么会出现这种低估——轻微的低估，即本科成绩有一个标准差的十分之一——大学理事会为此做过一项研究，他们通过结合专业选择（不同性别有所不同）以及女性在解开这个谜题时表现出的更高尽责性，成功解释了这一现象。最后，是变异性。在这里至关重要的一点是，因为方差的估计

cues.en: depend on the tails of the distribution, which by definition are less numerous. And since people at the tails are likely to be weeded out of many surveys for various reasons, it's important to have large representative samples from national populations. And for this, the gold standard is the science paper by Novell and Hedges with six
cues.zh: 取决于分布的尾部，而按定义，尾部的数据较少。由于处于尾部的人由于各种原因很容易在许多调查中被筛选掉，因此拥有来自全国人口的大型代表性样本非常重要。为此，黄金标准是 Novell 和 Hedges 的科学论文，其中包含六个

cues.en: large stratified probability samples in which they found that in 35 out of 37 tests, including all of the ones in math, space, and science, the male variance was greater than the female variance. One other gold standard data set is this graph of where the entire population of Scotland was given an intelligence test. What we have here
cues.zh: 大型分层概率样本，他们发现在 35 个测试（包括数学、空间和科学领域的所有测试）中有 37 个显示，男性的方差大于女性的方差。另一个黄金标准数据集是这张图表，其中对苏格兰全体人口进行了智力测试。我们这里看到的是

cues.en: This is IQ, where the mean is 100. And this is the proportion of men and the proportion of women. And as you can see, there's a very orderly finding. In the middle part of the range, females predominate, and both extremes, males slightly predominate. Needless to say, there's a large percentage of women at both ends as well, but there is also a sex difference. Now, the fact that these differences exist does not mean that they are innate. And this, of course, is a much more difficult question to answer.
cues.zh: 这是智商，平均值为 100。这是男性的比例和女性的比例。正如你所看到的，这是一个非常规律的发现。在中间段，女性占优势，而在两个极端，男性略占优势。不用说，两端也有很大比例的女性，但也确实存在性别差异。现在，这些差异的存在并不意味着它们是天生的。当然，这是一个更难回答的问题。

cues.en: A prelude is that nature and nurture are not alternatives. It is possible that the answer involves some of each. But I think that there are 10 kinds of evidence that at least suggest that the contribution of biology is greater than zero, though it is certainly nowhere near 100%. First is that there are lots of biological mechanisms by which a sex difference could occur.
cues.zh: 先说一个前提：天性与教养并非二选一。答案可能两者兼有。但我认为有10类证据至少表明，生物因素的作用大于零，尽管肯定远不到100%。第一，存在许多可能导致性别差异的生物学机制。

cues.en: There are large differences in sex hormones in men and women, especially prenatally in the first six months of life and in adolescence after puberty. There are receptors for hormones all over the brain, including the cerebral cortex. There are many small differences that have been noted in men's and women's brains, including the overall size of the brain, even correcting for body size, and the density of cortical neurons, cortical asymmetry, hypothalamic nuclei, and a number of others.
cues.zh: 男女在性激素上存在巨大差异，尤其是在出生前六个月的胎儿期以及青春期之后。大脑各处都有激素受体，包括大脑皮层。人们已经注意到男女大脑存在许多细微差异，包括大脑整体大小（即使校正体型后也是如此）、皮层神经元密度、皮层不对称性、下丘脑核团等许多方面。

cues.en: Many sex differences, certainly some, maybe all, are universal. The idea that there are cultures out there somewhere in which everything is the reverse of here turns out to be a myth. In human universals, the anthropologist Donald Brown surveying this literature points out that in all cultures, men and women are seen as having different natures, that there's a greater involvement of women in direct child care, more competitiveness,
cues.zh: 许多性别差异，当然是一些、也许全部，是普遍存在的。认为世界上某处存在一切都与这里相反的文化，这种想法其实是神话。在《人类普遍性》一书中，人类学家Donald Brown梳理相关文献后指出，在所有文化中，男女都被认为具有不同的天性，女性更多直接参与育儿，男性更具竞争性，

cues.en: in various measures for men and women, and a greater spatial range of men compared to women. In personality, there was at least a cross-national sample. In Feingold's meta-analysis, he noted gender differences in personality that are consistent across ages, years of data collection, educational levels, and nations. In terms of spatial and math abilities, I think we have less data. And the honest answer is that we don't have true cross-cultural
cues.zh: 在各项测量指标上男女存在差异，男性的空间活动范围大于女性。在人格方面，至少有一项跨国样本。在Feingold的元分析中，他注意到人格上的性别差异在不同年龄、数据收集年份、教育水平和国家之间都保持一致。在空间和数学能力方面，我认为数据较少。老实说，我们并没有真正的跨文化

cues.en: surveys, although we do have cross-national surveys. David Geary and Catherine DeSoto found these expected sex difference in mental rotation in 10 European countries, Ghana, Turkey, and China. And Diane Halpern analyzing results from 10 countries said that the majority of the findings show amazing cross-cultural consistency when comparing males and females on cognitive tests. Stability over time.
cues.zh: 调查，虽然有跨国调查。David Geary和Catherine DeSoto在10个欧洲国家、加纳、土耳其和中国发现了预期中的心理旋转性别差异。Diane Halpern分析10个国家的 results 后表示，在比较男女认知测试时，大多数发现显示出惊人的跨文化一致性。这种稳定性也随时间保持。

cues.en: In life interests and personality, there's been little or no change despite two generations of second wave of feminism. There is also, famously, resistance to change in communities that for various ideological reasons were dedicated to stamping out sex differences and found that they were unable to do so. These include the Israeli kibbutz.
cues.zh: 尽管经历了第二波女性主义的两代人，生活兴趣和个性几乎没有任何改变。同样众所周知的是，一些社区出于各种意识形态原因，致力于消除两性差异，结果却发现根本无法做到，并对此产生了抵制情绪。以色列基布兹就是其中之一。

cues.en: various rural American utopian communities of the end of the 19th century and contemporary androgynous academic couples. In mental rotation, the meta-analysis by Boyer et al. found no change over time. In mathematical reasoning, there has been a decline in the difference, although it has certainly not disappeared. cues.zh: 第六，被当作女孩养大的生理男孩。有一个著名的案例，有时被称为“约翰/琼案”。一对同卵双胞胎男孩中的一个在一次失败的割礼中失去了阴茎。我很欣慰地发现这不是由犹太割礼师做的，而是由一个笨拙的外科医生干的。在当时性别心理学家的建议下，父母同意对这个男孩进行阉割，给予女性

cues.zh: 特异性激素，并把他当作女孩抚养。这件事一直瞒着他，直到他14岁。我读本科时，这个案例作为性别角色完全是通过社会习得的例子教给我的。但事实证明，真相被隐瞒了。当这个男孩再次被回访时，事实证明，从很小的年纪起，他就

cues.en: Also, there's a widespread myth that teachers who, of course, are still disproportionately female, are actually dupes in perpetuating gender inequities, in failing to call on girls and otherwise having low expectations of their performance. In fact, Jessamine Eccles, in a study of 100 teachers and 1,800 students, concluded that teachers seem to be basing their perceptions of students on those students' actual performance and motivation.
cues.zh: 此外，还有一个广为流传的迷思，认为老师——当然仍然以女性居多——实际上是 perpetuating 性别不平等的帮凶，不点名女孩回答问题，以及对她们的表现期望过低。事实上，Jessamine Eccles在一项涉及100名教师和1,800名学生的研究中得出结论，老师似乎是根据学生的实际表现和动机来形成对学生的看法。

cues.en: She is, on average, better at reading emotions, body language, reading faces, better vocabulary, and better social skills. Just one note on stereotypes, and then I'll end. Are these stereotypes? Well, many of them are, although I must say not all, such as female abilities in spatial memory, mathematical calculation, and so on. There seems to be a widespread assumption in much of this discussion that
cues.zh: 平均而言，她更擅长解读情绪、肢体语言、面部表情，拥有更好的词汇量和更好的社交技能。关于刻板印象，我只说一点就要结束了。这些是刻板印象吗？嗯，很多是的，尽管我必须说并非全部，比如女性在空间记忆、数学计算等方面的能力。在许多关于此事的讨论中，似乎存在一种普遍的假设，即

cues.en: If there is a stereotype, that explains a difference as being the cause of differential expectations. But of course, the causal arrow could go in either direction. Stereotypes might reflect differences. And in fact, there's an enormous literature in cognitive psychology that says that people are good, intuitive statisticians.
cues.zh: 如果存在某种刻板印象，那就说明差异是由不同的期望所导致的。但当然，因果箭头可以指向任何一个方向。刻板印象可能只是反映了差异。事实上，认知心理学中有大量文献表明，人类是很优秀的直觉统计学家。

cues.en: and that their prototypes and conceptual categories track the statistics of the natural world pretty well. And that is, just as an example, we do have a stereotype that basketball players are taller on average than jockeys, but it certainly doesn't mean that our stereotypes cause that difference in height. Likewise, Alice Eagley and Jessamyn Eccles have shown that most of people's gender stereotypes are in fact pretty accurate. Indeed, the error is in the direction of under-predicting sex differences.
cues.zh: 并且他们的原型和概念分类能够很好地追踪自然世界的统计规律。举个例子，我们确实有一种刻板印象，认为篮球运动员的平均身高比赛马骑师更高，但这绝对不意味着我们的刻板印象造成了这种身高差异。同样，Alice Eagley和Jessamyn Eccles已经表明，大多数人的性别刻板印象实际上相当准确。事实上，误差的方向在于对性别差异的预测不足。

cues.en: So to sum up, I think there's more than a shred of evidence for sex differences that are relevant to statistical gender disparities in elite science departments. There are reliable average differences in life priorities, interest in people versus things, risk seeking, spatial transformations and mathematical reasoning, and variability in these traits. There are ten kinds of evidence that suggest that the differences are not completely explained by socialization and bias, although they surely are in part.
cues.zh: 总而言之，我认为有充分的证据表明，存在与精英科学部门中性别统计差异相关的性别差异。在生活优先级、对人与物的兴趣、求险倾向、空间Transformer（保留英文）与数学推理方面，以及这些特质的变异性上，存在着可靠的平均差异。有十类证据表明，这些差异并不能完全用社会化和偏见来解释，尽管部分原因确实如此。

cues.en: Just to give a couple of concluding thoughts, none of this, I think, provides any grounds for ignoring the biases and barriers that keep women out of science. As long as we keep in mind the distinction between fairness on the one hand and sameness on the other, they are different things. I'll give the final word to Gloria Steinem, who said that there are very few jobs that actually require a penis or a vagina, and all the other jobs should be open to both sexes.
cues.zh: 最后做几点总结，我认为这些并不能构成忽视将女性阻挡在科学界之外的偏见和障碍的任何理由。只要我们牢记公平与同质之间的区别——这两者是不同的概念。最后我用Gloria Steinem的话作结，她说实际上很少有工作非要阴茎或阴道不可，所有其他工作都应该对两性开放。

cues.en: Thank you very much.
cues.zh: 非常感谢。
